title: QB2_A#q31 claimed a personal fine-ore pre-loading routine the Founder cannot ground, published five unverified or wrong facts about a recent named casualty, and was the only reviewed card with no source-confidence block
candidate_claim: Founder/GPT Tranche-3 independent review, finding F-5 plus two attached authorisations. F-5: the 'On My Vessel' block asserted a personal fine-ore / concentrate pre-loading routine - confirming cargo declarations and TML certificates with the Chief Officer, checking the load-port weather record - on a candidate whose service is container vessels. Attached: this is the only reviewed card carrying NO source-confidence block of any kind, and the Founder/GPT governance ruling that a candidate-facing card publishing a recent named casualty with detailed factual claims must have a registered supporting source before release.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD ON ALL THREE, AND THE CASUALTY VERIFICATION FOUND MORE THAN THE RULING ASKED FOR. The ruling required each published fact to be verified individually. Doing so found THREE WRONG FACTS and TWO UNVERIFIABLE ONES in a card that read as careful and that already hedged in the right places - which is the point: the card's hedging was what made the errors invisible. The most instructive is the distance. The card hedged '230 to 240 nautical miles' and told the candidate that saying so meant they 'cannot be caught out'. No source supports 240. The genuine spread is about 230 (Reuters/Global Times) to about 290 (PTI via Outlook India). The hedge was on the WRONG SIDE of the disagreement - the same defect class as the National Shipping Board card that hedged after 31 August while the issuer's listing had moved five months earlier. A hedge that does not span the actual disagreement is worse than no hedge, because it advertises safety it does not have.

authority.regulatory_limbs: UNCHANGED and NOT re-opened: the IMSBC Group A / dynamic-separation definition, the TML rules, the Proctor/Fagerberg 70%/80% limbs and IMSBC Appendix 2, and the Casualty Investigation Code res. MSC.255(84) limbs (investigating State, substantially interested State, high-seas provisions, non-punitive character). These do not depend on the casualty and were outside the authorised scope.
authority.casualty_evidence: Registered as SRC-CASUALTY-OCEANWINNER-2026. THE DEFINING FACT ABOUT THIS ROW IS WHAT IT CANNOT OFFER. Panama is the flag State and therefore the marine safety investigating State under the Casualty Investigation Code ch. 6.2, and it has published NOTHING. India has published nothing. No owner or manager release was located. Tier 1 does not exist. The ruling's source preference was therefore worked down its own ladder to tier 2 (an official authority quoted in reporting - India's Director General of Shipping, and the Indian Coast Guard PRO) and tier 4 (contemporaneous reporting), with commercial ship registers used ONLY for vessel particulars. The card now says all of this to the candidate in as many words.
facts_verified_individually: Vessel identity: OCEAN WINNER, IMO 9145530, Panama flag, built 1998 - CORROBORATED across The Maritime Executive, Global Times and independent registers. IMO number ADDED to the card, per the ruling's allowance, because it is the only unambiguous identifier for a ship whose name is generic.
Ship type - bulk carrier, Panamax: VERIFIED.
Deadweight about 72,900 t (registers give 72,928; reporting rounds to '70,000 dwt'): VERIFIED and ADDED, replacing the unverifiable beam.
Load port Paradip, Odisha; sailed 20 August 2026: VERIFIED.

Sinking 21 August 2026 at about 1645 GMT: VERIFIED by two independent sources. The card's '21 or 22 August' hedge was resolvable and is now resolved in the body; the 22 August date belongs to the RECOVERY of the survivors, which is what the two dates in circulation actually are.

24 crew, 20 Chinese / 3 Myanmar / 1 Bangladeshi; 2 found, 22 missing: VERIFIED, and the nationalities ADDED because they are what makes the flag/coastal/substantially-interested-State analysis concrete.
The heavy list and 'about eight minutes': VERIFIED as the SURVIVORS' account relayed by India's Director General of Shipping. The card already attributed it that way and continues to.
Cargo iron ore fines: VERIFIED - and it is the fact the whole teaching connection rests on, so it was checked hardest.
Search coordinated by Indian Coast Guard MRCC with Indian Navy assets: VERIFIED; MRCC Beijing ADDED as joint coordinator.
Cause: NOT DETERMINED, no report published. VERIFIED as still true at 5 September 2026.
facts_corrected_or_removed: CARGO TONNAGE, WRONG: the card said 'roughly 72,100 tonnes'. No source supports it; reporting gives 71,200 tonnes. 72,100 is a transposition, and plausibly a corruption of the DEADWEIGHT 72,928 rather than of the cargo figure at all. Corrected to 71,200 and explicitly labelled 'a reported' quantity, because it is not a certificated one.

DISTANCE OFFSHORE, WRONG ON THE UPPER LIMB: '230-240 nautical miles' -> '230 to 290', the real spread, with the candidate now told to say 'something over two hundred miles, the reports differ' rather than a figure. The high-seas conclusion is unaffected and the card now SAYS it is unaffected - every reported distance is beyond the 200-mile EEZ - which turns a disputed fact into a demonstration of legal reasoning.

RESCUING VESSEL, WRONG: 'recovered from liferafts by a passing tanker'. No source supports a passing tanker. The verified facts are a liferaft and Indian Coast Guard Ship VARAD landing the two survivors at Paradip on 22 August. Corrected.
BEAM, UNVERIFIABLE: '32.26 m'. Registers give '32 m'. The false precision is removed and NO beam is now claimed - per the ruling, a fact that cannot be verified is removed rather than softened.
DESTINATION: reported as Singapore in some accounts and China in others. The card never asserted it and now says explicitly that it is disputed, so a later editor does not add it.

supersedes.note: Batch G2 created this card and pinned it. The pin is not rewritten and G2 is not rebaselined; its claim becomes ancestry. Full-sha256 convention on both sides.

changed_propositions: F-5, 'On My Vessel': the personal fine-ore / concentrate pre-loading routine REMOVED and replaced with the brief's own preferred pattern - state plainly that this is not a cargo operation from container-vessel experience, then answer from the applicable IMSBC requirements and from the list case, which IS the candidate's on any ship. The engineering content the old block ended with (bilge and ballast cross-connections, emergency generator on load, emergency fire pump priming) is KEPT, because that part was never a bulk-carrier claim.

15-second answer: IMO number and deadweight added; cargo tonnage 72,100 -> 71,200 reported; sinking date resolved to 21 August 2026 at about 1645 GMT; distance 230-240 -> 230 to 290; 'recovered from liferafts' -> found on a liferaft and landed at Paradip on 22 August.

Body 'Established' bullet: rebuilt on the verified set - IMO number, LOA and deadweight instead of the unverifiable beam, reported cargo tonnage, resolved sinking date and time, crew nationalities, ICGS VARAD, MRCC Beijing, the real distance spread, and an explicit warning that the destination is disputed.

Body 'Who investigates': 'At roughly 230 to 240 miles offshore' -> 'On every reported distance - the lowest is about 230 nautical miles - the casualty is beyond the 200-mile EEZ, so the dispute over the exact figure does not change the answer'. Found by a residual sweep AFTER the main edit, not by the original site list: the same wrong range appeared in a paragraph nobody had flagged.
Deep-dive 'Numbers to Memorise': the same five corrections carried through, so the memorisation layer cannot reintroduce the wrong figures.
Reg-box: 'Status as at 24 August 2026' -> 5 September 2026, and a NEW 'Source confidence' block added - see below.
cards.source_confidence_block: Added in the house pattern and deliberately structured in four parts. (1) The REGULATORY limbs and where they come from, flagged high confidence and independent of the casualty. (2) The CASUALTY facts, stating in terms that NO primary casualty source exists, that Panama has published nothing, and that everything factual comes from reporting or a commercial register. (3) What is DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED - no beam, no gross tonnage, no cargo certificate, no moisture content, no TML value, no owner, manager or class society, no cause - with the instruction that the right answer to a question about any of them is that it has not been established. (4) CURRENTNESS, naming the date and stating that an investigation report will supersede the whole factual half of the card and none of its regulatory half. It claims NO source was opened that was not opened, and it asserts no chapter or page structure of anything not read.
deliberately_unchanged: The question stem, which still reads 'sank off Paradip on 21/22 August 2026'. It is a hedge, not an error, and changing a stem moves the index display text and the workbook projection - which the brief's 'no Excel regeneration unless question identity or text changes require it' expressly discourages. The body now resolves the date. RECORDED as a decision, not an oversight, and referred to GPT.
The whole IMSBC / TML / Proctor-Fagerberg mechanism section, the Group A definition with its dynamic-separation limb, and the controls section. Read and correct; outside the authorised scope.

The Casualty Investigation Code analysis, including the point that India is a substantially interested State as the coastal State involved and NOT because the cargo loaded at its port. That is the card's best paragraph and it is untouched.
The CE Oral Tip, which already models the required judgement ('the word that matters is could') and closes soberly on the 22 missing seafarers.
The 'Where the Chief Engineer stands' section and the CE Relevance block.

propagation.scope_pass: Two sweeps. (1) The five corrected facts were re-grepped across the corrected card to prove zero residuals: '72,100' 0, '32.26' 0, 'passing tanker' 0, '230 to 240' 0 - the last only after the second-pass find described above. (2) A corpus-wide sweep for 'Ocean Winner' across all 86 files returns this card only, so no other card repeats any corrected fact.
found_and_not_swept: The governance ruling was applied ONLY to this casualty, on the brief's explicit instruction not to conduct a new corpus-wide casualty audit. Other cards carry named casualties (MOL Comfort, Ever Given and others) and were NOT audited for registered supporting sources. Whether the ruling extends to older, non-recent casualties is a question for GPT, not an omission of this pass.

meoclass1/index.html still reads 'Last Updated: 2 Sep 2026' and was DELIBERATELY not patched, on the brief's own instruction. No push, no deploy, no Excel distribution, no full release suite, no release-gate registration.
No regulatory proposition in the card changed. Every edit is to a fact about the casualty, to the provenance block, or to the 'On My Vessel' claim.

The card still states, in three places, that the cause is undetermined and that liquefaction is a hypothesis. Nothing in this correction converts the hypothesis into a finding, and the source-confidence block makes the absence of an investigation explicit.
No moisture content, TML value, certificate content, owner, manager or class society is asserted anywhere in the card.
